elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: Inserted section: "Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer and its Affiliates" — express defence duty running to Customer and its Affiliates (a defined term at § 1.1).

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: "...from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees)" in favour of "Customer and its Affiliates".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Limb (a): "an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right"; allegation-based trigger, no carve-out narrowing it.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: Limb (b): "Vendor's breach of Applicable Law", using the defined term at § 1.2.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Limb (c): "any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor". (Confirm "Customer Data" is the defined term used elsewhere in the Agreement; if the document uses a different label, conform the reference.)

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Limb (d): "Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct", consistent with the Excluded Claims language at § 21.3.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: "The indemnified party shall give prompt written notice of the claim".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: "the indemnifying party shall control the defence" — control is expressly allocated (reciprocally, so Customer controls under its own narrow indemnity).

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: "the indemnified party shall provide reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying party's expense".

elements.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: "Any Customer indemnity under this Agreement is limited to third-party claims arising from Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of Applicable Law." Drafted as a ceiling, not a grant, so it does not create a new Customer obligation.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-party claims.
elements.evidence: Limb (a) of the inserted section covers third-party allegations that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; the condition does not apply because no modification exclusion was inserted. Silence leaves the indemnity broader than the fallback contemplates, which is more favourable to Customer.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no combination exclusion was inserted, so the allowance is simply unused and the indemnity remains broader than the fallback tolerates.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no specifications exclusion was inserted — unused allowance, more favourable to Customer.

elements.element: Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: The inserted section contains no procure/modify/replace remedy ladder. This also leaves § 9.3's termination trigger ("cannot provide the remedies required by Section 20.5") without an anchor.

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: No refund-of-fees backstop appears in the inserted text or elsewhere in the cited paragraphs.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No cap language was inserted. Deliberate: § 21.3 already treats "its indemnification obligations" as Excluded Claims (uncapped), so omitting the 3x super-cap is Customer-favourable, but the fallback element is textually absent.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: Limb (a): "an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right" — Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer against such third-party claims.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: all ten preferred elements appear in operative text (defence duty, Customer plus Affiliates, IP/breach-of-law/Customer Data/gross negligence limbs, notice, defence control, reasonable cooperation, and a ceiling on any Customer indemnity). No element is left to the margin comment.

Fallback is incomplete (no procure/modify/replace ladder, no refund backstop, no 3x super-cap), but that is irrelevant to completeness because the preferred checklist is fully met, and the omitted fallback terms are Vendor-favourable concessions we are not obliged to volunteer.

Minimal: a single self-contained insertion at the gap between § 19.5 and § 21, adding no operative term outside the preferred checklist. It does not duplicate or disturb § 19.5 (disclaimer carve-out for indemnities), § 21.3 (indemnification obligations as Excluded Claims) or § 30.5 (indemnified-party enforcement and vested indemnity rights), all of which now have a referent.
Intent preserved: existing allocation, remedies and commercial mechanics are untouched; the insertion supplies the indemnity those provisions already presuppose rather than contradicting any of them.

Drafting defect to repair (does not defeat any preferred element): the inserted clause is rendered as an unnumbered "INDEMNIFICATION." heading. Number it "20. INDEMNIFICATION" (with numbered subsections) so § 9.3's cross-reference to "the remedies required by Section 20.5" is not left dangling; alternatively amend § 9.3 to refer to the new Section 20 generally, or add a 20.5 procure/modify/replace/refund subsection — otherwise the IP-infringement limb of our § 9.3 termination right depends on a non-existent provision.

Secondary conforming check: verify "Customer Data" in limb (c) matches the Agreement's defined term (the definitions supplied resolve Affiliate, Applicable Law, Fees, Order Form, Services and Excluded Claims but not Customer Data); if the document uses a different label, align the reference so limb (c) is not left with an undefined object.

Optional, not required for completeness: consider adding a consent-to-settlement proviso (no settlement admitting Customer liability or imposing non-monetary obligations without Customer's consent). This is a preferred-wording nicety, noted rather than treated as a gap.
Severity remains critical as scoped — the pre-redline document had no Vendor IP indemnity at all, which is walk-away territory; the insertion cures it at the preferred level.
